nativeRvaLock.note: The behaviour hooks are Harmony patches declared by interop type and member name, so no test locks these RVAs. This file is the build-specific record of the members the behaviour facts read.

extraction.tool: scratch extractor outside the repository (Il2CppDumper dump.cs + Iced)
extraction.callEdges: rel32 call opcode scan over .text and il2cpp, accepted only when the relative target is a declared method of a wanted type

hookMembers.name: UpdateTargets
observations: called by every awake behaviour update: 21 EB_*.UpdateBehaviour bodies (EB_Patrolling, EB_Patrolling_Investigate, EB_InCombat, EB_InCombat_MoveToPoint, EB_InCombat_MoveToTarget, EB_InCombat_MoveToNextNode, EB_InCombat_Pouncer_MoveToTarget, EB_InCombat_MoveToPoint_Flyer, EB_InCombatFlyer, EB_InCombatFlyer_FlyOutOfBoss, EB_Dash_Pouncer, EB_PlayerHeld_Pouncer_Base, InCombat_ChargedAttack, EB_SquidBoss_Hibernating, EB_SquidBoss_Intro, EB_SquidBoss_Combat, EB_SquidBoss_Raging, EB_SquidBoss_Cooldown, EB_SquidBoss_RageTransition, EB_SquidBoss_Spawning)
also called by EnemyAI.Setup at 0x155EE1A and EnemyDetection.Setup at 0x1569F97, which is what makes the state an enemy spawns in observable as a baseline

EB_Hibernating.UpdateBehaviour does not call it: a sleeping enemy in EB_States.Hibernating is sampled at setup and again on its first awake behaviour update, which is exactly the sample that carries the wake-up
the postfix reads EnemyDetection.m_ai at +0x18 only; the body itself writes no behaviour fact

hookMembers.name: OnTargetRegistered
observations: 3 callers, all scout tendril paths: ScoutAntennaDetection.RegisterTarget at 0x158C63D, ScoutAntenna.RegisterTarget at 0x158F556, ScoutAntenna.DetailUpdate at 0x158E810
the body writes the target it was handed: m_detectionType at +0x6A becomes 3 and the byte at +0x86 becomes 1, so a postfix observes the target in its registered shape
the body does not write AgentTarget.m_agent (+0x18) or AgentTarget.m_position (+0x30): both come from the registering caller
the postfix reads ES_ScoutDetection.m_owner at +0x68 (the EnemyAgent) and the target argument

hookMembers.name: ChangeState
observations: writes m_currentStateName at +0x99 only when the incoming state differs (cmp [rdi+99h],bl; je), so a native state write is always a transition

7 callers: EnemySync.IncomingState at 0x1580A6A (state replicated from the master), ES_DeadBase.Enter at 0x16DD49D, ES_Hitreact.DoHitReact at 0x16E2F73, ES_HitreactFlyer.DoHitReact at 0x16E18AC, EB_Patrolling_Investigate.UpdateBehaviour at 0x17F1C6B, ES_HibernateWakeUp.Exit at 0x17FDAC3, ES_ScoutScream.CommonUpdate at 0x1801D9A
ES_HibernateWakeUp.Exit is the wake-up path, so leaving hibernation is a real state transition and not only a locomotion state
hookMembers.usedBy: read only: the pump reads EnemyBehaviour.m_currentStateName, it never calls ChangeState

hookMembers.name: UpdateData
hookMembers.visibility: private in the game; the interop assembly exposes a public wrapper
observations: calls Mathf.Clamp01 at 0x156A16E, so the detection build-up it maintains is a 0..1 quantity
2 callers: EnemyDetection.UpdateHibernationDetection at 0x156AD0C and EnemyDetection.UpdateInCombatDetection at 0x156BADC

hookMembers.name: UpdateHibernationDetection
observations: 3 callers: EB_Hibernating.UpdateDetection at 0x166C60B, EB_Patrolling.UpdateDetection at 0x17F29AD, EB_Patrolling_Investigate.UpdateDetection at 0x17F1CFA
this is the detection path a hibernating enemy runs; it never reaches UpdateTargets
hookMembers.usedBy: documents why a sleeper's alert watermark only advances when it next runs the frame pump

hookMembers.name: UpdateInCombatDetection
observations: calls UpdateData at 0x156BADC, EnemyDetection.IsTargetValid at 0x156BC78, Mathf.Clamp at 0x156BD5E and 0x156BE2F
hookMembers.usedBy: documents that the alert quantity stays bounded in the combat path as well

hookMembers.name: ActivateState

hookMembers.name: CommonUpdate

hookMembers.name: OnDead

hookMembers.name: DoDamage

a second implementation exists at 0x161C6F0 in a limb subclass
no rel32 caller was found in the scanned sections, so the call path into it is indirect

hookMembers.name: NotifyLimbDestroyed

hookMembers.name: OnEnemyKilledMaster
observations: a static delegate field, not a method: the game invokes it indirectly, so a rel32 scan cannot see the call sites

its payload GlobalCallbacks.EnemyDamageInfo is a struct with DamagedAgent at +0x0, Source at +0x8, Damage at +0x10, Position at +0x14, Direction at +0x20, Hitreact at +0x2C, TryForceHitreact at +0x2D, LimbID at +0x30, StaggerDamageMulti at +0x34, DamageNoiseLevel at +0x38 and gearCategoryId at +0x3C (dump lines 558539-558553)
10 subscriber methods named OnEnemyKilledMaster exist on other types (dump lines 528742-529474)

interopConfirmation.note: The interop assembly exposes even the private natives UpdateData and IsTargetValid as public wrappers, so the visibility recorded on those two rows is the game's own declaration from dump.cs. Every member the behaviour observer reads was confirmed in this assembly, which is the assembly the native plugin compiles against.

hostAuthority.rule: Every behaviour fact is published by the master only.
evidence: state replicated from the master arrives through EnemySync.IncomingState, which calls EnemyBehaviour.ChangeState at 0x1580A6A: a client's behaviour state is a follow of the master's, so a client-side publish would duplicate or contradict the host's fact
the module's publish path is gated on SNet.IsMaster, and the pump returns before reading native state when the gate is closed

ports.state: EB_States mapped to the catalog ai_state member

evidence: ChangeState writes the field only when the value differs, so a native write is a transition
the spawn state is a baseline, not a transition, because EnemyAI.Setup and EnemyDetection.Setup call UpdateTargets once before any behaviour update
one publish per observed transition; a repeated identical read publishes nothing

conclusions.member: the same state field, published only when the previous sampled state was EB_States.Hibernating (0) or EB_States.SquidBoss_Hibernating (12) and the new one is not
evidence: ES_HibernateWakeUp.Exit calls EnemyBehaviour.ChangeState at 0x17FDAC3, so leaving hibernation is a behaviour state transition
EB_Hibernating.UpdateBehaviour never calls UpdateTargets, so the sample that carries the wake-up is the first awake behaviour update
conclusions.catalogGap: the catalog declares a cause entity port; no native member names a wake-up cause, so the port is not registered

evidence: EnemyDetection.UpdateData clamps the build-up with Mathf.Clamp01 at 0x156A16E, so the value is a 0..1 quantity
quantization keeps a continuous ramp from publishing on every behaviour update
conclusions.catalogGap: the catalog declares a threshold input; a trigger may not declare input ports (RuntimePlan 'trigger-shape'), so the threshold belongs in the consuming plan as a comparison step

conclusions.member: AgentAI.IsTargetValid and AgentAI.Target, sampled by the same pump

ports.target: the target resolved through the kernel's instance resolvers, absent when unresolved

evidence: EnemyDetection.IsTargetValid at 0x1569E80 is the native judgement the combat detection path uses, so validity is not re-derived
conclusions.catalogGap: the catalog declares target as a required entity port; it is registered nullable and optional because a valid native target may be no registered kind (ruling 50: an unresolvable port is absent, never a null placeholder)

conclusions.member: the same validity transition, in the lost direction

ports.target: the last resolved target, absent when the host never named one

evidence: validity and the target struct are read in the same stable sample, so acquire and loss are ordered by the game's own detection update
conclusions.catalogGap: the catalog declares a reason string port; no native member exposes a loss reason, so the port is not registered

ports.target: the detected agent resolved through the kernel's instance resolvers, absent when unresolved
ports.position: the native target position in metres

evidence: 3 registering callers (ScoutAntennaDetection.RegisterTarget, ScoutAntenna.RegisterTarget, ScoutAntenna.DetailUpdate) all pass through this member
the body sets the target's detection type to 3, so the hook runs after the game accepted the target

conclusions.member: ES_ScoutScream.m_state (+0x68), read only while EnemyLocomotion.CurrentStateEnum is ES_StateEnum.ScoutScream (13)
evidence: ES_ScoutScream.ActivateState (0x1801890) is called from EB_Patrolling.UpdateDetection and EB_Patrolling_Investigate.UpdateDetection
the state object survives its exit, so the locomotion state gates the phase
conclusions.catalogGap: the catalog declares phase as an enum with schema command_phase (requested/accepted/committed/rejected/cancelled), which is a command lifecycle vocabulary and does not describe Setup..Done; the port is registered as an integer carrying the native member value

limb_damaged.bestMember: Dam_EnemyDamageBase.ProcessReceivedDamage (0x137E570): damage, damageSource, limbID and the hit position are all parameters, and 6 channel receivers call it
limb_damaged.secondaryMember: Dam_EnemyDamageLimb.DoDamage (0x13840F0): the per-limb application, 7 instructions, subtracts from m_health at +0x44 and returns whether the limb dropped below zero
limb_damaged.gap: DoDamage has no rel32 caller in the scanned sections, so a hook must sit on ProcessReceivedDamage and use limbID (-1 means no specific limb)

staggered.bestMember: none: no native stagger event, method or field was found
availableSignals: staggerDamageMulti is a parameter of Dam_EnemyDamageBase.ProcessReceivedDamage

staggered.gap: no duration and no stagger-specific event exist; a staggered fact would have to be derived from damage parameters plus a state observation
